description: Partnerships Promote Healthy Forests and Clean Water is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Aurora Water; Coalition for the Upper South Platte; Coca-Cola Company. Two major fires and subsequent flooding events wreaked havoc on a critical watershed and reservoir that supplies Denver with water. Now, a public-private partnership is working to ensure a clean, reliable water supply. Coverage: the United States (2014). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: For decades, forest caretakers across the West followed a strategy of fire suppression: when branches broke off or trees died, the wood accumulated in forests, leading to heavy fuel loads. Combined with severe drought—a condition that occurs more frequently in our warming climate—wildfires in fuel-laden forests can burn very hot, destroying vegetation and the topsoil’s ability to hold water.
